- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.09) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at +2% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.3) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought signals.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust down by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment drops to 0.00, model often fails to recognize bearish momentum; add 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment to forecast to reflect subdued market sentiment.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag: if true outcome is below 70, model often misses the drop; apply early correction by 1–2% on day 1–3 of the forecast window.
